meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'so that, in order to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'a hundred', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thousand' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'otherwise', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Go, or else you'll be late.

examples.text: Пятьдесят метров, не больше. Иначе будет сигнал.
examples.trans: Fifty metres, no more. Otherwise there'll be a signal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to speak'.

examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-другому').

examples.text: И будут общаться со мной по-другому.
Я серьёзный мужчина! И будут общаться со мной по-другому.
examples.trans: I'm a serious man! And they'll treat me differently.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'лноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry'.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'occupy, take up'.

examples.text: Да, это занимает очень много моего времени.
examples.trans: Yes, it takes a lot of my time.

examples.text: И денег нам занимать не нужно.
examples.trans: And there is no need to lend us money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'uh-huh, yeah', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common feminine noun meaning 'hospital' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take', paired with 'брать'.

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'волноваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get nervous, worked up'.

related.gloss: not to to get nervous (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: Why are you getting so worked up?

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет разволноваться без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to get nervous without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'ten', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to lay down', paired with 'класть'.

examples.text: В гроб с собой икру не положишь!
examples.trans: You can't put caviar in your coffin to take with you!
Put the keys on the table.

examples.text: А вот сюда я её и положу! Отличный подарок будет!
examples.trans: Right here is where I will put it! It will be an excellent gift!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.
